fluid_domain.evidence: Fluid network only (not the column range): the 298.15..900 K caloric fit continued to 293.15 K (the bundled ambient continuation qualified in the fluid-network batch, with the pure-component viscosity tables sampled from 293.15 K); 100 Pa..10 MPa: every phase at its own pressure (P3 WP4 direct path), and above its 293.15 K floor methane (Tc 190.56 K) is a supercritical gas outside every declared critical-band box (P3 WP7); PR78 density +0.95 % at 300 K and 10 MPa against the Helmholtz reference (P1 study section 2.5). Viscosity above 2 MPa is a reference-pressure value.

freezing.source: ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Methane" (ChemSep index 1, CAS 74-82-8): melting point, triple point temperature and pressure, heat of fusion at the melting point. Data only: never a validity floor or a range end.

thermochemistry.source: Ideal-gas heat of formation at 298.15 K and formula CH4 (molar mass 16.043 g/mol) of ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Methane" (ChemSep index 1, CAS 74-82-8). Heats of reaction follow by Hess's law. Data only.

flammability.source: M. G. Zabetakis, Flammability Characteristics of Combustible Gases and Vapors, US Bureau of Mines Bulletin 627 (1965), Table A-1, p. 115, entry "Methane": L25 and U25 in air at 25 C and atmospheric pressure. A US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105). Constant with temperature (owner decision E23).

combustion.source: Hess's law on this record's thermochemistry (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1): the formula burnt to CO2, H2O (gas), SO2 and N2 on the ideal-gas heats of formation at 298.15 K of icheme:chemsep_carbon_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1), icheme:water (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1) and icheme:chemsep_sulfur_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1). Computed by tools/heating-values/heating-values.mjs. Read by a fired heater's burners.
